children: Saudi Arabia's crude oil shipments in September jumped to the highest level since the start of the Iran war, Bloomberg reported Thursday, after the country accelerated exports through the Strait of Hormuz following the attack on its key East-West pipeline two weeks ago.

Overall Saudi exports reportedly jumped to 5.28M bbl/day so far in September, the highest rate since February and up sharply from August, when shipping was disrupted from the country's eastern and western facilities.

The shipments coincide with booming sales, as Saudi has sold nearly 100M barrels of crude to Asian customers since the middle of last week for delivery in October and November, Bloomberg also reported, helping to avert a looming supply crunch in the region.
The sales flurry would more than double the recent flows of Saudi crude from the Hormuz route to Asia, according to Bloomberg estimates.

The report comes as Saudi Aramco is in the early stages of restarting the pipeline and is aiming for a meaningful restoration of flows by the end of this week, although full resumption of the conduit's 4M bbl/day capacity likely will take weeks.
Bloomberg also reported that Qatar has ramped up liquefied natural gas tanker traffic through Hormuz to the highest in more than two months.

Oil futures rose more than 2% on Thursday as diplomatic talks between ‌the U.S. and Iran showed little sign of progress, while investors focused on uncertainty about a potential U.S. ban on diesel exports.
